Portable source distribution of **Unity** ([ThrowTheSwitch/Unity](https://github.com/ThrowTheSwitch/Unity)), a lightweight unit test framework for C, designed for embedded targets. This repository is consumed by the Embedbits Platform Artifact Handler to locate, download, verify, and configure Unity in downstream embedded projects — typically together with the **CMock** artifact (mock generation) and the **Ruby** artifact (interpreter for the CMock / Unity generator scripts).

This repository is split into three branches/refs by role — the `main` (`master`) branch you are reading now holds only this documentation; the handler scripts live on the `Core` branch, and versioned source packages are published as GitHub Releases anchored to the `Bin` branch.

---

## Repository contents

```
main / master
└── README.md                     ← This document — no other content

Core
├── ArtifactConfig.cmake          ← Artifact metadata (name, version constraints, asset naming)
└── CMakeUnityDefaults.cmake      ← Unity integration logic (library target / include setup)

Bin  (anchor branch — no tracked binary files)
└── (empty commits only; each release tag points here)
```

---

## Role in the platform

```
GitHub (ThrowTheSwitch)                   GitHub (Embedbits)
──────────────────────────────────────    ──────────────────────────────────────────
ThrowTheSwitch/Unity                      Artifact-unity
  tag "v2.6.1" (source)               ──►    main / master →  README only (this document)
                                              Core          →  ArtifactConfig.cmake, CMakeUnityDefaults.cmake
                                              Bin           →  Anchor branch (empty commits)
                                              Releases      →  unity-<version>.zip + .hash
                                                                tagged Bin/<version>
```

`Unity_Importer.sh` clones the upstream repository at each release tag (`vX.Y.Z`, release candidates are ignored), verifies the checked-out tag, strips `.git` metadata, adds a plain-text `VERSION` file, and zips the source tree. Unity is portable C source compiled straight into the test project, so releases carry **no platform suffix** — they are tagged plainly `Bin/<version>` (the `v` prefix is dropped).

---

## Branch structure

| Branch / Ref | Content |
|---|---|
| `main` / `master` | This README only — no functional content |
| `Core` | CMake handler scripts for consuming the artifact |
| `Bin` | Anchor branch only — no binaries are committed here |
| Release tag `Bin/<version>` | GitHub Release carrying the `.zip` source package and its `.hash` checksum file |

> **Note:** On a Git host without a Releases API (Azure DevOps), the same importer commits the `.zip` + `.hash` directly to the `Bin` branch and tags that commit `Bin/<version>`. The CMake handler resolves either form transparently.

---

## Fetching a release

```bash
# Core handler scripts
git clone --branch Core --single-branch --depth=1 <repository_url> unity-core

# Source package + checksum for one specific version (GitHub Release asset)
gh release download Bin/2.6.1 --repo Embedbits/Artifact-unity --pattern "unity-2.6.1.*"
```

---

## Package layout

```
unity-<version>.zip
└── unity/
    ├── VERSION                   ← plain-text version, e.g. "2.6.1"
    ├── src/                      ← unity.c, unity.h, unity_internals.h
    ├── extras/                   ← optional add-ons (fixture, memory, bdd)
    ├── auto/                     ← Ruby helper scripts (test runner generator, ...)
    └── ...                       ← upstream docs, examples, build files
```

The Ruby scripts in `auto/` (e.g. `generate_test_runner.rb`) require a Ruby interpreter — use the **Ruby** artifact.

---

## Versioning

Artifact versions correspond directly to **official Unity release tags** with the `v` prefix removed:

```
2.5.2, 2.6.0, 2.6.1, 2.7.0, ...
```
